column3: MT 6:3. Close to the Aramaic; “overseers” is rendered “governors,” and “not suffering injury” “would suffer no loss.”
MT 6:4. Close to the Aramaic; “was planning” is rendered “gave thought to.”
MT 6:7. Close to the Aramaic; “they came as a crowd” is rendered “thronged.”
MT 6:8. Close to the Aramaic; the list of officials is rendered “governors … administrators and satraps, the counselors and advisors,” and “prohibition” “a firm decree.”
MT 6:11. Close to the Aramaic; “three times in the day” (that is, daily) is rendered “three times that day.”
MT 6:12. Close to the Aramaic; “they came as a crowd” is rendered “assembled.”
MT 6:15. Close to the Aramaic; “it was displeasing to him” is rendered “was greatly displeased with himself.”
MT 6:17. Close to the Aramaic; the wish “may he deliver you” is rendered as a statement, “He will deliver you.”
MT 6:19. NKJV renders the uncertain word glossed “thrusting [women]” as “musicians”; the meaning is uncertain.
MT 6:24. Close to the Aramaic; “he had trusted” is rendered “he believed.”
MT 6:25. Close to the Aramaic; the idiom “who had eaten the pieces of Daniel” is rendered “who had accused Daniel.”
MT 6:28. Close to the Aramaic; “the hand of the lions” is rendered “the power of the lions.”
